recommendation_reason: Only protection for a wrong-ownership fixture-isolation invariant and the body is cheap; the 28-binary execution is a cost/consolidation observation, not a reason to drop value.
overlap_notes: Body executes once per including test binary: 28 inventory rows (for example ovrcr::automatic_titles ... ovrcr::workspace_identity), all with identical source_start 568 and source_end 579 and equivalent contexts, so the 28 executions are one coverage unit. behavior: A Followup accepted at control epoch 1 with a reserved contract loses its response (proxy armed, ControlRule loss 2, fault followup-after-files, 360-364); after human takeover/return/confirm reaches epoch 4, re-sending the accepted request is Rejected with identity and result_version preserved and result_version still 1, byte_count unchanged, and repeating it is idempotent (same receipts, same byte count). criticality_reason: The behavior guards delegation authority and durable assignment state: a replayed followup runs a continuation under revoked control (wrong ownership of the assignment) and can apply a contract the human explicitly replaced, with receipts, versions and brief/contract files as the durable record.
signal_reason: Precise state-preserving positive and negative assertions: DispatchOutcome::Rejected with identity/result_version equality (396-403), `fixture.byte_count(&original) == before` twice (405, 413), `again.receipts == recovered.receipts` (412), result_version 3 while contract stays 1 (420-427), execution_attempts Some(1) across complete/reconcile (428-438, 459-467), reserved file bytes unchanged (440-447, 469-472), and the negative collect of version 2 (473-486).

fidelity_reason: Real binary Server, real managed PTY, real on-disk briefs and contracts, real ovrcr_followup/ovrcr_collect tool dispatch; the only substitution is the acceptance-diagnostics proxy that manufactures the lost response.
recommendation_reason: Dense high-value coverage of a subtle durable-state defect; the medium confidence reflects that a full 259-test cross-comparison was not performed.
overlap_notes: Gated on #[cfg(feature = "acceptance-diagnostics")] (control.rs:352-353). Neighbouring fresh/stale epoch test shares helpers (transition/confirm/settled) but not this failure mode.

anchor: node:a late startup reply cannot restore a retired factory
behavior: createDelegationContinuation (production src/ovrcr-delegation-continuation.mjs, imported by src/ovrcr-pi-runtime.ts:18) issues a Recover on session_start; while that promise is unresolved a session_shutdown with reason reload retires the factory; when the reply finally resolves, continuation.state stays null, continuation.gap matches /retired/, and no pointer entry is appended.
failure_caught: A late Recover reply restoring workflow authority state, handles and pointer into a session factory that was shut down or reloaded, so a retired session acts on stale delegation authority.
criticality_reason: Restoring authority after retirement gives a reloaded or forked session control of a workflow it no longer owns (wrong ownership of an assignment), and the restored pointer/handles would drive later delegation writes.
signal_reason: Three precise post-race assertions: `assert.equal(f.continuation.state, null)`, `assert.match(f.continuation.gap, /retired/)`, `assert.equal(f.appended.length, 0)` (73-75) reject resurrection, silent dropping without a recorded gap, and a pointer append; the fixture also records restored/resets (line 11) which this test leaves unasserted.
uniqueness_reason: Other cases in the same file cover fork/new non-inheritance (33-41), malformed pointers (43-52) and failed publication (54-64); the late-reply-after-shutdown ordering is a distinct race and is the only case that retires a factory mid-call.
fidelity_reason: Runs the real production continuation module through its event-handler API (pi.on handlers, before_agent_start/session_*), with the pi host and the Recover call supplied as fixtures; the extension wiring (src/ovrcr-pi-runtime.ts) is not exercised, which is outside this race.
recommendation_reason: Decisive timing-boundary assertions on a stale-authority race in production code, 0.00027 s.
overlap_notes: 119-line file; nearest ancestor behaviour is the fork/new reset test (33-41), which asserts resets=[true] and state null under a different trigger.

behavior: Launch the compiled bridge in --client mode with stdin piped and left open and no bytes written; the child must exit within 2.5 s, elapsed must satisfy 1.5 <= dt < 2.5, returncode must be 0 with empty stderr, and stdout must be exactly one JSON line {"schema":…, "server_wire":…, "status":"failed"}.
failure_caught: The compiled client losing its open-stdin deadline (hanging until killed, or never answering), answering with a different status or extra output, or admitting a request from an incomplete stdin before the deadline.
criticality_reason: The client is spawned per notification by the bridge; a lost deadline hangs that delivery path with no in-app recovery short of killing the child, and the same guard is what keeps an incomplete request from being admitted (check-guards.py:77-78 comment).
signal_reason: Assertions at 82-86 combine the timeout window (1.5-2.5 s), exit code 0, empty stderr, and the exact single-line protocol payload with status failed; together they reject returning immediately, hanging, wrong status, and extra output. The one gap is that no IPC attempt is observed directly, so the 'before IPC' part of the claim is inferred from the status and the guard design.
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from wrong-profile-open-stdin-exits (100-109), which requires exit in under 1 s for a profile mismatch (a different authority state), and from the closed-stdin check() matrix (38-75); no other check leaves stdin open with no request.
fidelity_reason: Real compiled binary, real pipes, real clock and real JSON protocol; the OS process boundary is the subject, so the full boundary is exercised.
recommendation_reason: Real-process guard check with precise exit and payload assertions; the timing window is part of the asserted behavior, not a measured flake input.
overlap_notes: Inventory has production and local-development rows with the same 78-94 range and identical assertions apart from the --local-development profile; the profile is a distinct authority state for the neighbouring wrong-profile check, not for this one.
